links.outcome: Time to palliative care consult/order, ACP notes, palliative diagnosis codes vs control
links.effect: Time to 0.1% ordered 42.8 vs 63.9 days (posterior >0.99); consult completed 60.9 vs 71.8 days (posterior 0.88); ACP note and Z51.5 code unchanged (effects 1.04 and 1.03).
links.quote: However, the intervention had a smaller effect on the time to the palliative care consultation, indicating that considerable barriers to timely consultations still existed.

links.outcome: Positive predictive value of algorithm presentations (top 40 weekly)
links.effect: PPV 0.18; specialists accepted 273/1512 cases presented across both arms.
links.quote: In this trial, the algorithm had a PPV of 0.18, with the palliative care specialist accepting 273/1512 cases presented across both arms.

models_evaluated: Mayo Clinic machine-learning algorithm predicting palliative care needs

links.outcome: Time to palliative care consultation orders after risk-based identification and specialist-confirmed eligibility
links.effect: Time to 0.1% having consultation orders was 42.8 (34.5–54.2) days with the intervention versus 63.9 (46.8–90.1) days with control; posterior probability of shorter time, > 0.99.
links.quote: The median (95% credible interval) time to 0.1% of the population having the consultation ordered was 42.8 (34.5–54.2) days for the intervention arm and 63.9 (46.8–90.1) days for the control arm (posterior probability of a shorter time with the intervention, > 0.99; Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: Positive predictive value against specialist assessment of consultation appropriateness
links.effect: PPV was 0.18; specialists accepted 273/1512 presented cases. Nonacceptance could reflect already-addressed needs or unsuitable referral timing, rather than absence of palliative care needs.
links.quote: In this trial, the algorithm had a PPV of 0.18, with the palliative care specialist accepting 273/1512 cases presented across both arms.

links.outcome: Clinician-reported mismatch between referral alerts and patient-care timing
links.effect: Among 28 responding PCPs (response rate, 30%), 6 (21%) reported that alert timing did not align with patient care; 2 (7%) disagreed with the recommendation.
links.quote: In some instances, alert timing did not align with patient care ( n = 6 [21%]) or the PCP disagreed with the recommendation ( n = 2 [7%]).

models_evaluated: internally developed machine-learning algorithm for palliative care prediction

links.outcome: time to 0.1% population palliative care consultation
links.effect: 60.9 days for the intervention compared with 71.8 days for the control
links.quote: For the primary outcome of time to a palliative care consultation, the median (95% credible interval) time to 0.1% of the primary care adult population receiving the consultation was 60.9 (47.8–79.4) days for the intervention, as compared with 71.8 (50.9–103.8) days for the control (posterior probability of a shorter time with the intervention, 0.88; Fig. 2 ).

links.effect: 24.6% of patients presented were accepted, 67.6% snoozed, and 7.7% excluded
links.quote: Of the 934 patients presented, 230 (24.6%) were accepted at least once, 631 (67.6%) were snoozed, 72 (7.7%) were excluded, and 1 (0.1%) was never reviewed (lack of provider time).

links.effect: 75% of respondents found the alert helpful
links.quote: Most respondents ( n = 21 [75%]) found the alert helpful: 4 (14%) rated it as “extremely” helpful, 7 (25%) as “very” helpful, and 10 (36%) as “moderately” helpful.

unlisted_practices: Interposing a specialist clinician to review AI predictive alerts before notifying primary care providers to filter out inappropriate alerts.
